findings.summary: R14: /components/* is outside both the proxy matcher and its owner-page predicate; entry pages have no independent session check. Anonymous requests can read catalog entry content. See T25.md F1 and probe A.

R14/R15: agent-index.ts writes llms.txt at public/llms.txt, which the proxy allows anonymously, and never writes the required public/r/llms.txt. The required token-protected text index is missing while its contents are public at another path.

R1/R4/R6: internal registry dependencies are frequently bare names. The installed shadcn resolver sends card, use-motion and tokens to ui.shadcn.com, rather than @david-ui. This installs upstream variants or fails on unavailable upstream items. See probe B.

R6: registry installation flattens UI files but preserves source-tree-relative imports. shadcn's own planner/import rewriter leaves Aurora importing ../effects/lifecycle despite planning components/ui/lifecycle.tsx; Showcase and Toast have analogous broken imports. See probe B.

R3/R8 and inventory section 6: tokens.css is never imported by the application, globals.css defines the stock grayscale palette without mapping to --du-* tokens, and no loaded stylesheet defines the profile duration variables. The intended Catppuccin theme and token-backed motion are not integrated.

R5/R6 and US-6: all twelve Bencho baseline candidates remain pending in resolvedEntries and none has a registry item. resolved.ts imports neither Bencho update module; the capabilities module only exports origin notes. Implemented files are therefore undiscoverable/uninstallable as the twelve required kit entries. See probe C.

R5 and final acceptance: catalog/check.ts ignores --final and does not reject pending candidates or require registry presence. npm run catalog:check -- --final exits 0 while twelve baseline entries remain pending. The final gate can report success on an incomplete requirement.

R9: 49 validated entries lack an EntryDemo mapping. Their catalog entry iframe goes to /demos/entry/<id>, whose route calls notFound for those entries, including Calendar, motion capabilities and React Bits. Standalone group demos do not repair the broken entry-page previews. See probe C.

R9: EntryPage's install command installs only npm dependencies when any are present, otherwise contains the literal <registry-url> placeholder. Neither branch installs @david-ui/<id>; the acceptance browser test explicitly asserts this incorrect command.

R9: EntryPage renders an API-summary paragraph instead of a props/API table, and its states section lists state names rather than showing a states gallery. There is also no theme toggle on the entry page.
R9 and inventory section 11.5: no gaps route or catalog panel lists Comparison Slider, Device, Page Flip, AI Blob with states, Modal Cards, Hover Preview, or unavailable entries with their reasons.

US-7/R6 and inventory section 11.1: all nine text-effect exports are static wrappers around TextEffect, which always renders the full text in one span. There is no typing, decryption, shuffle, grouped reveal, changing focus, scroll-velocity response or pointer-proximity deformation, despite validated status.

US-7/R6 and inventory section 11.2: showcase exports are hardcoded sample projects and controls rather than reusable presentations accepting consumer content/data. CircularGallery lacks a curved image gallery/expansion, Masonry lacks animated media/lightbox, MagicBento lacks pointer lighting, CardSwap lacks a rotating 3D pile, and StaggeredMenu reveals items instantly. Entries are nevertheless validated.

R13: the performance test disables WebGL for every browser, samples generic requestAnimationFrame for 1500 ms instead of each background for 5 s, computes no median, applies no 30 FPS threshold and implements no measured mobile-default fallback. It cannot support validation of WebGL-enabled mobile rendering.

R6/R13: the CSS implementing all six effects and five backgrounds, including the static fallback, is only in src/app/globals.css. Their registry items ship TSX files without that stylesheet or equivalent css metadata, leaving installed components without their appearance/fallback positioning.

US-7 and inventory sections 11.3-11.4: PixelTransition exposes only one children surface with a hover gradient and cannot transition between content through pixels. All five backgrounds use the same generic sine-wave/glow shader with different fixed tints and no pointer input; DotGrid has no animated dots and Orb/Silk/Aurora lack their selected interactions.

SPEC Edge cases: VoiceNote never invokes getUserMedia or MediaRecorder and has no recorded media output. With default props it reports Recording and Voice note saved without accessing a microphone; its demo only forces a denied state. See probe D.

R12 and inventory section 10.2.2: RollingNumberInput renders minus/output/plus controls with no editable input. It cannot receive a typed numeric value, contrary to the required distinction from passive CountingNumber. See probe D.
US-6: UploadDropzone advertises dropping files but implements only input onChange, without dragover/drop handlers. Dropping a valid PNG produces no acceptance callback or state change. See probe D.

R12: SloshSlider hardcodes step=1 and exposes no step prop, narrowing the shared Slider contract instead of preserving value/onValueChange and min/max/step. It also changes the documented array-valued Slider interface to a scalar wrapper without an explicit shared contract.

R3/R6/R8: overlay implementations use fixed duration-150/200 CSS scale/height transitions without reduced-motion overrides or profile variables. P2 Drawer/Collapsible/Progress also retain fixed profile-independent durations. P1 reduced-motion tests check a provider attribute, not that these transitions collapse.

R4: the kit-only guard omits motion/@animate-ui imports and raw dialog, and does not scan src/demos, where real raw buttons are rendered by the catalog. In-memory violation fixtures for motion/react, @animate-ui/react and dialog all return no findings, while a button control is caught. See probe E.

R5/R10: copied-source version fields contain descriptions such as shadcn/ui registry (new-york, fetched 2026-10-23) and React Bits ... source pinned 2026-10-23, without an upstream release version or commit. Dates alone cannot identify the upstream source needed for deliberate re-diff/update.

R5/R10: sources explicitly described as clean-room in Bencho variants and React Bits effects/backgrounds retain copied-source metadata: origin inventory, route copy, copiedFiles and a fabricated upstream-version description, rather than the required own/inspiredBy provenance. Bencho variant updates also use the observed public-demo date as an upstream version.

R6 and T24a acceptance: acceptance.mjs delegates to registry-smoke.mjs, which installs only @david-ui/button. There is no per-source/all-installable-entry loop, no consumer render/import of other entries, and runAcceptance never invokes the browser catalog flow. The harness cannot establish the required full production acceptance.

R6/R13: WebGLBackdrop locates its host with document.querySelector by background name rather than its instance ref. Rendering two Aurora instances creates two canvases in the first instance and none in the second; the in-memory React/jsdom probe returned [2, 0].

R10: repository AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md describe consumption but omit the required upstream-update procedure (identify pinned version, re-diff against local adaptations, review and deliberately apply changes instead of overwriting).

R3 and inventory section 11.6.8: Showcase embeds sky/amber/violet/emerald colors; background wrappers embed RGB tint arrays and effect/fallback CSS embeds fixed hex colors. Changing kit theme tokens cannot replace those tints even after the missing token import is repaired.

R6: overlay demos provide one normal trigger/content instance, without the declared disabled/pressed/focus/hover state gallery. buildP1QaUpdates nevertheless copies applicableStates into demoStates and marks every overlay validated; p1.spec.ts does not assert those states exist.

R3/R8: CountingNumber and AutoHeight are direct @animate-ui/react re-exports. Their installed upstream code uses its own explicit spring/useTempoTransition; the kit neither wraps them with active-profile transitions nor supplies AnimateUIProvider tempo. Switching kit motion profile therefore does not control these capability timings.

US-6 and inventory section 10.1: PickerWheel is an ordinary Select with three hardcoded sizes and no wheel interaction; SloshSlider is an ordinary Slider with an output and no fluid presentation; CreateMenu is an always-visible group of three buttons rather than the selected expanding contextual menu. These implementations lack their selected differentiating behavior.
